note: SPEC-terrain §14.1 — the single carrier of the RENDERED FORM of kogaki's owner surfaces. Where SPEC.md's prose and this artifact disagree about the rendered form, THIS ARTIFACT WINS (§14.1), from the moment it exists and not before. It governs the rendered form and nothing else: not which members are placed, not what a claim says, not whether a figure is honest, not §2.1's family-naming duty. Those remain SPEC.md's prose.

encoding_choice.chosen: a line-class grammar expressed in JSON
encoding_choice.why: Every rule §14.2 makes decidable is a statement about a LINE — its class, its token shapes, and whether its class is admitted on the surface at all. A JSON Schema describes a data structure; the artifact these emitters produce is text, and the thing being constrained is the text. Expressing line classes directly means an emitter validates what it is about to print rather than a model of it, which is the distinction §14.2's own AC3 rests on.
encoding_choice.declined: JSON Schema — checkable by tooling already present in this repository (checks/check-terrain-composition.sh validates survey records against survey-schema.json), but it would require modelling rendered Markdown and terminal text as a document tree first, and that model would itself be an unchecked restatement of the format.
encoding_choice.recorded_here_because: SPEC.md §14.1 names this file and its duties and deliberately does not decide the encoding (story 1.52 SQ1). A choice made in implementation and left unwritten is one the next editor re-derives.

LessonDisplayID.means: a member's owner-facing display id, assigned once in the survey record (§14.3)
LessonDisplayID.pending_producer_note: The emitters render `lesson:<slug>` at v14 (terrain/terrain.mjs:471, :719, :842, :993, :1177, memberBlock :1731). This grammar is therefore STRICTER THAN THE CODE until story 1.53 lands, and story 1.54's emit-time refusal must not be enabled against this token before then. Declared here rather than discovered at 1.54's first run.

GroupID.renders_today: the co-tag name itself, an arbitrary served tag string (terrain/terrain.mjs:658, `g.name`/`g.cotag`)

LessonCount.means: a count of Lessons, family-named per §9

Cite.shape: a served-surface citation string, rendered inside backticks
Cite.means: provenance — the address a served rendering was quoted at
Cite.status_under_14_3: UNDECIDED HERE, deliberately. A first draft of this artifact asserted that a cite is not an element name and so falls outside §14.3's no-names duty. That was a narrowing of a ratified owner duty (§14.3, kogaki#318 — the duty binds all six surfaces) made in a file that wins on divergence, with no §14.3 warrant and no record on the licensing issue. Withdrawn. This artifact takes no position: whether a served cite string may render on an owner surface is kogaki#345's question (story 1.53 SQ2 already carries it, over memberBlock's `*Served line:*` row at terrain/terrain.mjs:1736), and it is answered there or on kogaki#318, never here.

SubstratePin.shape: a substrate pin string, rendered inside backticks

JudgePin.means: model_id/effort_tier, or the typed literal `none` (§12.1 uniform arity)

cotag_screen.non_member_fallback: REFUSE — a line whose class is not in line_classes is not rendered and the emitter refuses to print (§14.2). The fallback is refuse and never admit, because an enumerated prohibition's non-member fallback is admit and that is the shape §9 chose against.

line_classes.form: <tag> — the second navigation step. Grouped by co-tag; sort: <COTAG_SORT>.
pinned to <n> member(s) — a subset selection RECOMPOSES and re-offers it as a gate event (SPEC.md §7)
judged by <model_id> / <effort_tier> (§6.2 — a judged surface with no judge pin is the drift-undetectable shape)
ABNORMAL: <n> of <m> group(s) on this screen carry no composed GroupClaim. …
Compose them from the bounded input — compose-input --survey <F> --tag <T> — …
Cover: <n> of <m> member Lessons appear in at least one co-tag group — counted AFTER composition, over placements. Selected tag: <strandFigure>; <denominator>.
Select a group (still narrowing nothing): cotags --survey <F> --tag <T> --group "<co-tag>"

line_classes.note: The emitters separate blocks with empty lines — a trailing \n on the header (:661), the post-judge-pin blank (:725), and the \n-prefixed subgroup and cover lines. A grammar that admitted no blank line would, under REFUSE, reject every screen the emitter produces.

line_classes.form: COTAG_COVER_INCOMPLETE — <n> member(s) of <tag> appear in no co-tag group: <ids>. …
line_classes.note: A refusal message is owner-facing text on this surface and is admitted as its own class. It is not a defect being tolerated: it is §2.1's cover invariant announcing itself.

line_classes.form: COTAG_COVER_INVENTED — <n> id(s) appear in a co-tag group without carrying "<tag>": <ids>. …

full_report.medium: Markdown, the owner rendering of §12.2 v11

line_classes.form: *The judgment produced NO split — this is a judged-empty outcome, not an absent judgment. Members are listed below.*

levels.when: under ## SubGroups on the JUDGED-EMPTY path, where no ## Members heading is emitted at all

line_classes.levels_note: Three cases, not two. The judged-empty path is the one an enumeration drops, and §12.1 v9 exists precisely to keep a judged-empty outcome distinguishable from an unjudged one — a refusal built from a two-case reading would reject exactly that report.

line_classes.note: renderReportMarkdown interleaves L.push("") between every block (terrain/terrain.mjs:1652-1702). Admitted for the same reason as the screen's: under REFUSE, a grammar with no blank-line class rejects every report the emitter writes.

uncovered_surfaces.note: SPEC-terrain §14.1 defines an OWNER SURFACE as any text this runtime prints or writes for the owner to read, and enumerates six. This grammar covers two. The four below carry §14.3's duty — no element name on an owner surface — with NO MECHANICAL CARRIER. Named here so a reader can tell 'not covered' from 'not thought about' (story 1.52 AC1b).
uncovered_surfaces.reopen_trigger: the first format defect observed on any of the four, or the first grammar edit that could have covered one and did not (§14.1)

members.renders: screen 1 — the survey listing: tag rows, candidate rows, Gloss headlines

declared_allowlist_not_enforced_here.source: specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §9 (v5, kogaki#147), transcribed verbatim in meaning and not reinterpreted
declared_allowlist_not_enforced_here.note: §9's allowlist is the one already stated in prose, and it governs SCREEN 1's tag rows — which cmdView renders, not cmdCotags. It is recorded against its true surface rather than moved to a covered one; see reader_notes.ac2_surface_mismatch.

members.renders: the composed claim and its member pins (:842)
the adopted claim and its member list (:993)
the subdivision specimen, including per-SubGroup member ids (:1177)

decidable_rules.note: SPEC-terrain §14.2's enumeration. Each is decidable on the rendered text alone, which is what makes the emit-time refusal possible. A rule that is not mechanically decidable does not enter this artifact and stays prose.

expressible.rule: zero occurrences of the literal `lesson:`, and zero element-name tokens in a MEMBER-NAMING position — the member lists on `group_heading_flat` and `subgroup_heading`, and `member_heading` on the report
expressible.scope_note: Scoped to member-naming positions rather than 'anywhere on the surface'. The wider form and tokens.Cite gave story 1.54 two readings it could not both implement: a served cite string is not a member name, and whether it may render at all is undecided (tokens.Cite.status_under_14_3). The narrow rule is the part this artifact can decide; the residue is carried, not silently resolved.

expressible.rule: every token in a member-list position matches tokens.LessonDisplayID
sum of LessonCount over a group's `subgroup_heading` lines == the LessonCount on its `group_heading_subdivided` line
the Lesson count of the group named "(no second served tag)" divided by the Cover line's member denominator <= 0.30
a line whose class is not in the surface's line_classes ⇒ REFUSE

not_expressible.why: There is no G/SG identifier to give a shape to. Group names are the co-tag strings themselves and SubGroup names are judge-composed prose (terrain/terrain.mjs:658, :1087); no `G<n>`/`SG<n>` space is minted anywhere in this repository. A token shape asserted here would be a rule about artifacts nothing can produce — a conformance category with no members, which reads as coverage.
not_expressible.carrier_of_the_missing_half: kogaki#317 (indentation-encoded hierarchy replaced by Group/SubGroup IDs) and kogaki#314-#316, all open
not_expressible.reopen_trigger: the sitting that mints the G/SG ID space adds tokens.GroupID and tokens.SubGroupID here and moves this entry into `expressible`

reader_notes.ac2_surface_mismatch: Story 1.52 AC2 asks that `the grammar's cotag_screen tag-row entry` match SPEC.md §9's allowlist. The co-tag screen renders NO tag rows: §9's allowlist governs SCREEN 1's tag rows, produced by tagRow() at terrain/terrain.mjs:407 and printed by the survey/view path — which §14.1 lists as `cmdView`, an UNCOVERED surface. The allowlist is therefore transcribed against cmdView above, where it actually binds, rather than attached to a surface that has no such line class. Transcribing it onto `cotag_screen` would have satisfied the AC's letter by reinterpreting the rule, which is the one thing AC2 forbids. Reported on kogaki#344.
reader_notes.completeness_of_the_line_classes: The classes were read off the emitters, and the round-1 review of kogaki#349 found the first draft admitted no blank line and neither COTAG_COVER refusal — which, with non_member_fallback REFUSE and §14.1's precedence, is a grammar that rejects every render the code produces. Both are now classes. The general hazard stands and is stated rather than claimed away: this enumeration is only as complete as the read that produced it, and a class discovered missing is found by story 1.54's refusal rejecting a valid render. Story 1.55's golden fixture is what converts that from a live-run discovery into a CI one.
reader_notes.what_this_artifact_is_not: Not a second carrier beside the golden fixture (§14.5) — the fixture never wins against this file; precedence is one-way. Not an enforcement mechanism — story 1.54 installs the emit-time refusal that reads this. Not a description of §13's provenance neighborhood, which is unimplemented and whose display-id question is a named deferred slot (§14.6, kogaki#300).
